PRODUCT: Timex T231W2 AM FM Dual Alarm Clock Radio with 1.2-Inch Green Display and Line-In Jack White. REVIEW: I bought this clock about a week ago. Several reviewers have mentioned that the display on this clock is too bright, even when the display dimmer is used. Personally, I don't think the dimmed display is all that bright. The nice thing is, I no longer use my bedroom nightlight for the times I have to get up to answer nature's call. My nightlight was brighter, but this clock casts an adequate glow on the ceiling. The OTHER problem mentioned by reviewers is that, with the exception of the 34 snooze 34 bar, the REST of the control buttons are all the same size, and very small, and so are hard to distinguish one from another, especially when you are trying to operate the alarm functions in the dark. The control button design IS poor, and you shouldn't have to do what I did, but it works, and for the price of this otherwise decent clock, it was worth the effort. I simply purchased a pack of those little rubber-like, self-adhesive, pea-sized, cushioning beads available at Wal-Mart, Target, hobby stores, etc. and stuck one bead to each of the 2 alarm buttons. Voila! NOW I can feel the alarm buttons in the dark without wondering what function I am about to change, and with the 2 now-easy-to-feel alarm buttons as 34 home base, 34 in the dark I simply count buttons to whichever other function I want to operate. Works perfectly. I suggest wiping the alarm buttons with a little rubbing alcohol first, to help the beads to stick better. Other than this, I am very happy with this clock. And, really, the big, bright display makes it easy to see the time when your eyes are clogged with sleepiness in the middle of the night.

The two go very well together and the NAD has no trouble at all driving them in my medium large room. Since I'm not an audio reviewer it's difficult for me to articulate why I like these speakers so much, and I don't just want to regurgitate a bunch of stuff I've read in speaker reviews. With that said, these speakers are pretty tonally neutral. Highs are pleasant, not harsh at all. The midrange is also very pleasing to my ears. Low end is very satisfactory to me, but I'm sure others would want to pair this with a sub. I've noticed that these speakers have no trouble resolving recordings with lots of bass In fact, like all good speakers, these sound best with good records, but they are more than fair to lesser quality records. One cool thing about the 220's is that they have a downward firing bass port and this means they can be placed pretty close to a wall, which helps bass response. Vocal clarity is the one thing that really jumps out at me with these speakers. The vocals are crisp and right in the middle of the soundstage. TV dialogue also has the same vocal clarity. Overall a great set of speakers.
